messages:
anya: Quick heads-up — after flipping FP8 KV on the staging cluster last night, we see a measurable regression in decode quality (more hallucinations, coherency drops) on our long-context chat tests. ppl went from ~12.8 -> ~14.6 on eval-set.

sam: Can you paste the perf/profile traces and the exact config you used for KV?

anya: Sure. Config used: `kv_quant: fp8`, `kv_scale: per_head`, `kernel_pref: auto`, batching defaults (max_batch=64, max_tokens=4096). Spawned a 2k-seq load with 8 concurrent streams.

anya: Paste of perf sample (reduced):
```
# staging-run-2025-11-12
p50_token_latency: 28.2 ms
p95_token_latency: 67.1 ms
p99_token_latency: 112.8 ms
mem_kv_bytes_per_request: 24.8 MB (was 39.2 MB with fp16)
decode_ppl: 14.6 (was 12.8)
roc_auc_quality_drop: -6.2% on safety/eval prompts
```

kevin: Interesting — memory drop looks good ( ~37% ), and token latency p50 improved slightly, but p99 is similar. Where's the extra decoding error coming from? Could be calibration/scales for FP8 underflow/overflow on KV reads or a mismatch between quantized KV format and chosen attention kernel.

maria: Also check batching: with FP8 we changed kernel selection heuristics earlier (we prefer 4-bit/FP8 fused kernels for long sequences). If kernel selection flips between steps (quantized KV used but attention kernel expects fp16 cached KV), we might be inserting dequant/ requant steps at runtime. That could add tiny numeric noise every step — compounding across long decodes.

anya: I captured a flamegraph and a short trace showing extra `dequantize_kv` calls around decoder step 64+. Attaching snippet:
```
# trace excerpt
00:00.000 GPU: qkv_load (fp8)
00:00.012 GPU: dequantize_kv (fp8->fp16) x 8 calls
00:00.048 GPU: attention_fused_fp16 (select)
```

sam: Can you repro with a deterministic small test? e.g., single stream, seed + prompt, compare fp16-kv vs fp8-kv decode tokens and per-token logprobs. If the logprob differences start small and accumulate, it points at repeated dequant noise.

anya: Did that. I ran 50 deterministic streams for 512 tokens. Summary:
- fp16-kv (baseline): mean token logprob trace stable
- fp8-kv (current): per-token delta mean ~ -0.02 logprob per token after token 120, cumulative divergence causes wrong top-1 choices on 8% of sequences.

kevin: That cumulative -0.02/token fits the hypothesis. Two possible culprits: (1) FP8 scale calibration is off (per_head vs global), causing quantization dynamic range clipping; (2) kernel selection chooses mixed-precision attention kernels that do an extra quant/dequant.

kevin: Quick checks: 1) Re-run with `kv_scale: per_tensor` (coarser) and `kernel_pref: force_fp16_attention` to force no dequant. 2) Try INT8 KV (our INT8 impl uses asymmetric quant + zero-point) to compare behavior.

anya: I ran both:
- fp8 + force_fp16_attention -> ppl 13.0 (still slightly worse than fp16 but much closer), p99 latency +8ms
- int8_kv -> ppl 13.8, memory savings ~31%, p50 latency similar, p99 slightly better than fp8 (no hopping between kernels)

maria: So forcing fp16 attention removed the repeated dequant noise but cost a bit of latency. That suggests the problem is the mixed kernel path inserting repeated conversions. We may be able to add a kernel selection rule: prefer attention kernels that accept quantized KV directly (no dequant) or prefer consistent precision across the whole decoder stack.

kevin: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: add a runtime invariant that KV precision must match attention kernel input precision. If mismatch detected, prefer attention kernel that matches KV (even if slightly slower) to avoid multi-step quant/dequant.

anya: I can push a staging patch to `runtime/kernel_router` that checks `kv_precision == attention_in_precision` and penalizes kernels that force conversions. Also add a quick perf test harness to measure per-token logprob drift for 1k tokens.

sam: Also add calibration experiments. I suspect our `per_head` FP8 scales were computed with shorter calibration sequences. Try recalibrating with longer contexts (>=1024 tokens) and with a representative prompt mix. Past work showed FP8 needs wider calibration samples to avoid underflow later in generations.

anya: I'll run a calibration matrix overnight: [per_head, per_tensor] x [calib_len: 128,512,2048] x [sample_count: 256,1024]. Will post results tomorrow AM.

perf-bot: Deploy check: staging patch queued by anya. CI: unit tests ok. Canary route to 5% will run once kernel change landed. :robot_face:

maria: Long-term we should add a numeric regression alert tied to eval prompt sets that includes per-token KL and top-1 flip rate. If KL drift > threshold after quant change, fail the rollout. Current rollout didn't have that guard.

kevin: Yep — add runtime flags and an automatic re-run of a small deterministic eval on any quant or kernel change. If cumulative token logprob delta > 0.5 across 512 tokens -> block.

anya: Update: quick overnight matrix (partial results):
- fp8 per_head calib128 samples256 -> ppl 15.1 (bad)
- fp8 per_head calib2048 samples1024 -> ppl 12.9 (close)
- fp8 per_tensor calib2048 samples1024 -> ppl 12.7 (best)
- int8 per_channel calib512 samples256 -> ppl 13.6

anya: So far best result was FP8 with per_tensor scale and large calibration set. Memory win ~35%, p50 latency similar, p99 +10-12ms vs pure fp16. Quality ~on-par.

sam: Great. Action items: (1) revert staging rollout to use `kv_quant: fp8` + `kv_scale: per_tensor` + `kernel_pref: avoid_mix` (anka will add flag name) (2) implement kernel selection invariant in next PR (3) add numeric regression check in release pipeline.

anya: I'll open PRs for (1) and (2) this morning and add the eval job for (3). Will attach the overnight calibration logs to the PR.

maria: Thanks — also add a short docs note in `eng-runtime/quant` describing expected tradeoffs (latency vs memory vs required calib size) so SRE and DS know how to tune for different SLAs.

anya: Cool. I'll include calibration artifacts and a small script `tools/compare_logprob.py` that diffs deterministic decodes and computes cumulative drift.

kevin: One more note — test INT8 KV with our newer asymmetric kernel that avoids zero-point corrections; it may close the gap further. If int8 gives similar quality with smaller mem, might be preferable for most customers.

anya: Will add INT8 asymmetric to matrix. Thanks all.

sam: :thumbsup: Keep thread updated when PRs land and when canary finishes.
